description: Fix response shape mismatch between backend paginated response and frontend expectations. The backend UserController::index() returns paginatedResponse() which wraps data in { success, data: { items: [...], pagination: {...} }, message, timestamp }. The frontend does setData({ users: result, loading: false }), treating the whole response as the array. Frontend must extract result.data.items (or result if the outer envelope is unwrapped by apiClient).
steps: In resources/js/shared/api/client.js, check if apiClient.get() already unwraps the outer { success, data, message } envelope and returns only data. Read the interceptor logic.

If apiClient returns the full envelope, modify UserManagementPage.jsx loadUsers() to extract result.data.items instead of treating result as the array. If apiClient already unwraps to data, then extract result.items.
Also extract result.data.pagination (or result.pagination) and store it in state if pagination UI is planned, or ignore it if the page does not paginate
Update the mock in resources/js/shared/mocks/manager/users.js to return the same shape as the real API after client unwrapping, so mock and API modes behave identically
acceptance_criteria: When VITE_DATA_SOURCE=api, the user table displays users from result.data.items (or result.items if apiClient unwraps)
When VITE_DATA_SOURCE=mocks, the user table displays the same structure from mockUsers
No console errors about undefined or incorrect data structures
verification: Run the app with VITE_DATA_SOURCE=api and confirm the user table populates correctly
Run the app with VITE_DATA_SOURCE=mocks and confirm the user table populates correctly
Open DevTools console and confirm no errors about undefined .items or .data
